title: South Bend population 1,652 (1850 census)
description: Earliest South Bend count collected: 1,652 in 1850, 3,832 in 1860, 35,999 in 1900 and 104,193 in 1930 (decennial counts as tabulated in Wikipedia).

title: Studebaker begins making wagons in South Bend
description: H.C. Studebaker begins making wagons and horse-drawn buggies in South Bend, later automobiles (City of South Bend 2024 ACFR narrative).

title: City of South Bend incorporated
description: South Bend was incorporated as a city on May 22, 1865; William G. George was elected its first mayor that year.

title: First Common Council elected
description: The first South Bend Common Council was elected on June 5, 1865 (Wikipedia, citing Howard's history of St. Joseph County).

title: Studebaker workers organized as AFL Local 18310
description: Studebaker workers organized as AFL Local 18310, later UAW Local 5, per the UAW Region 2B history page (seen in a search summary only).

title: Sit-down strike at Bendix Corporation, South Bend
description: The UAW Region 2B history page describes a sit-down strike at Bendix on this date as the first sit-down strike in America. This is the union's characterization; a historian's source is needed before publication.

title: South Bend reaches its peak census population
description: South Bend had 132,445 residents in the 1960 census, its highest count. By 2020 the city had 103,453 (about 22 percent fewer) while the county grew from 238,614 to 272,912 (about 14 percent more).

title: Mayor Edward Voorde dies in office
description: Mayor Edward F. Voorde died in office on September 2, 1960; Frank J. Bruggner became acting mayor and did not seek election in 1963. How Bruggner was selected was not confirmed.

title: Studebaker ends production in South Bend
description: Studebaker's South Bend plant ceased production on December 20, 1963 (last Avanti December 26); the engine block plant closed in 1964. Sources report about 7,000 local jobs affected, but plant employment figures are inconsistent across sources.

title: Lloyd M. Allen re-elected mayor; last Republican elected mayor of South Bend
description: Republican Lloyd M. Allen was re-elected mayor in 1967 with 58 percent. Every mayor elected since has been a Democrat.

title: 1971: Jerry Miller (D) elected mayor
description: Democrat Jerry Miller won the 1971 mayoral election, beginning continuous Democratic control of the office. He campaigned on a cabinet form of government and restructured the executive branch after taking office.

title: Lowest South Bend mayoral turnout since 1925
description: The 1979 mayoral general election drew 29,196 votes, the lowest since 1925 (Wikipedia, citing the South Bend Tribune).

title: Bob Kovach elected mayor of Mishawaka
description: Bob Kovach (D) won the 1979 mayoral election, defeating Republican Margaret Prickett, who had won four terms from 1963 (South Bend Tribune). He served one term, 1980-1983.

title: AM General wins initial Humvee contract
description: AM General won an initial $1.2 billion contract in March 1983 for 55,000 Humvees; the Mishawaka plant was built in 1984 and production began that fall. LTV Corp. bought AM General in 1983.

title: Robert Beutter elected mayor of Mishawaka
description: Robert Beutter was elected in 1983 and served as mayor from 1984 to 2003, five terms; WSBT and the city describe him as the longest-serving mayor in Mishawaka's history.

title: Closest modern South Bend mayoral general election
description: Joe Kernan defeated Carl Baxmeyer 53 percent to 47 percent (17,030 to 15,104) in 1987.

title: Ball Band (Uniroyal) plant in Mishawaka closes
description: The Ball Band (Uniroyal) plant in Mishawaka closed in 1997 after import competition (Wikipedia).

title: Kernan leaves mayor's office for lieutenant governor; Luecke fills vacancy
description: Mayor Joe Kernan resigned after being elected lieutenant governor in 1996; council member Steve Luecke was appointed unanimously by the council (single secondary source) and was then elected in 1999, 2003 and 2007.

title: County unemployment rate reaches 11.4 percent annual average
description: BLS LAUS annual-average unemployment for St. Joseph County was 11.4 percent in 2009 and 11.2 percent in 2010, the highest annual values in the 2000-2025 series.

title: Dave Wood becomes mayor of Mishawaka after Jeff Rea resigns
description: Mayor Jeff Rea resigned in 2010 to lead the South Bend Regional Chamber; Dave Wood (R) finished the term and was elected in 2011, 2015, 2019 and 2023.

title: Newsweek lists South Bend among 'America's Dying Cities'
description: Newsweek published its 'America's Dying Cities' list, on which South Bend appeared, on January 21, 2011 per New America; Notre Dame Magazine reportedly dates the list to 2010. The article itself was not obtained.

title: Indiana House Democrats leave the chamber over right-to-work bill
description: A group of 37 Democrats, led by Rep. B. Patrick Bauer of South Bend, left the Indiana House in February 2011, saying they aimed to block a right-to-work bill; they returned on March 28, 2011. Daily fines rose from $250 to $350 during the walkout. The General Assembly passed a right-to-work law the next year, signed February 1, 2012.

title: Police recordings dispute leads to litigation against the City of South Bend
description: In 2012 Mayor Pete Buttigieg (D) demoted police chief Darryl Boykins amid a dispute over recorded calls. The city later settled suits with Boykins ($75,000) and with officers ($500,000 combined); on May 28, 2026 a federal judge ruled for the officers and ordered the recordings destroyed.

title: Pete Buttigieg takes office as mayor of South Bend
description: Pete Buttigieg (D) won the 2011 general election with 73.85 percent and took office on January 1, 2012.

title: County population 272,912; South Bend 103,453 (2020 census)
description: St. Joseph County had 272,912 residents in the 2020 census; South Bend 103,453 and Mishawaka 51,063.

title: James Mueller takes office as mayor of South Bend
description: Mueller, a Democrat and former chief of staff to Buttigieg, took office on January 1, 2020 after winning the 2019 election with 63.40 percent (official canvass: 9,406 to 5,429).

title: Commissioners adopt new commissioner district maps
description: The Board of Commissioners voted 2-1 on November 16, 2021 to adopt new maps for the three commissioner districts (Andy Kostielney and Deb Fleming yes, Derek Dieter no); state law requires council districts to fall within them. Kostielney said the maps keep communities of interest together and 'removed the political process from these maps'; Dieter said the process was rushed and lacked public input. Council members said they might sue (WVPE).

title: County Council overrides commissioners' veto of its redistricting ordinance
description: The County Council passed a three-map council redistricting ordinance in December 2021. The commissioners vetoed it on December 29; Kostielney objected that it was 'based on a series of events that we don't even know the answers to.' The council overrode the veto 6-3 on December 30. Council members who backed the ordinance said the commissioner maps placed most of the county's Black voters in one district and were unconstitutional (WVPE).

title: Commissioners and council settle the redistricting suit
description: Council members had sued the commissioners at the end of 2021, arguing the commissioner maps packed most of the county's minority voters into one district and that the county's 2020 population took it out of its special redistricting process. WVPE reported on March 1, 2022 that both boards had passed amended maps under a mediated settlement approved by an Elkhart County Superior Court judge, ending the challenge to the state law. County officials could not provide the litigation cost; the council had voted in November 2021 to hire Ice Miller for up to $100,000 (WVPE).

title: Republican caucus selects Carl Baxmeyer as commissioner
description: A Republican caucus chose Carl Baxmeyer in August 2022 to fill the District 1 commissioner seat vacated by Andy Kostielney, who resigned; Baxmeyer was elected board president 2-1.

title: Republicans win a 5-4 majority on the County Council
description: Republicans won a 5-4 majority on the nine-member County Council in November 2022; the council had been 6 Democrats and 3 Republicans. WNDU described it as the first Republican majority; that 'first' was not independently verified.

title: AM General wins JLTV A2 production contract
description: AM General won a U.S. Army Joint Light Tactical Vehicle A2 production contract worth more than $8.66 billion in February 2023 (Wikipedia).

title: Democrats win all nine South Bend Common Council seats
description: Democrats won all nine council seats in the 2023 municipal election. District 5 was decided 1,414 to 1,376 (38 votes) in a district that had elected Republicans since at least the early 1990s (WVPE).

title: Republican caucus selects Tony Hazen as District 3 commissioner
description: Tony Hazen was the only candidate at the January 20, 2024 Republican caucus after Deb Fleming's retirement took effect January 31, 2024. He won the November 2024 election with 58.50 percent (22,491 votes).

title: Amazon Web Services announces data center investment near New Carlisle
description: AWS announced an investment of about $11 billion for a data center campus near New Carlisle; the state said at least 1,000 jobs, and Gov. Holcomb called it the largest capital investment announcement in Indiana's history (AP). Construction reportedly began in September 2024 (third-party tracker; no official status found).

title: Narrowest county row-office results in the 2024 general election
description: Official 2024 results: Recorder decided by 81 votes (54,038 to 53,957) and Surveyor by 172 votes (54,375 to 54,203).

title: UAW Local 5 members ratify new AM General contract
description: About 400 UAW members at the Mishawaka complex ratified a contract with a 12 percent wage increase over three years, per the UAW. The figure is the bargaining unit, not total plant employment.

title: Court rules on the county election structure; appeal pending
description: In February 2023 the City of South Bend and two county voters, Warren and Iris Outlaw, sued the State of Indiana Election Commission in Marion Superior Court 11 (cause 49D11-2302-PL-005795). The complaint challenges the state laws that give St. Joseph County district-only elections for commissioners and for the county council, including the changes House Enrolled Act 1285 of 2022 made to the population range in IC 36-2-2-4(c) and 36-2-3-4(c). It argues they are special legislation barred by Indiana Constitution Article 4, sections 22 and 23, and that they also violate Article 1, section 23 and Article 2, section 1. In April 2023 the Election Commission moved to dismiss. ABC57 reported that the motion argued the Commission does not run or enforce the law, so it was the wrong party to sue, and that the plaintiffs had not shown any actual harm. In May 2023 the City amended the complaint to add as defendants the St. Joseph County Board of Commissioners and commissioners Carl Baxmeyer, Deb Fleming and Derek Dieter, the St. Joseph County Council and its members, and the St. Joseph County Election Board (ABC57, May 22, 2023; court docket). The defendants opposed the claims: the docket shows their cross-motion for summary judgment and a joint reply in January 2025. The text of the briefs is not posted on MyCase, so the guide does not describe either side's arguments beyond the complaint and the motion to dismiss. The court held a bench trial on Feb 6, 2026 and entered final judgment on Apr 14, 2026 (amended Apr 21, typo fixes only). The court record lists the challenged statutes as IC 36-2-2-4(a)(2) and (c), 36-2-2-5(d)(2), 36-2-3-2(b) and 36-2-3-4(a)(2) and (c). The order's text is not posted publicly, so its scope is known only from news reports: ABC57 reported on Apr 22, 2026 that a judge ruled the district method of electing commissioners violates the free-and-equal-elections guarantee, and 95.3 MNC reported on May 14, 2026 that the county council passed a resolution encouraging the county to appeal "a recent Indianapolis judge's ruling" on the nine-member council structure, which the station described as finding that structure illegal. The Election Commission and other defendants appealed to the Indiana Supreme Court (26S-PL-00156, filed May 14, 2026); the appeal was fully briefed on Oct 2, 2026 and is pending. The Nov 2026 election was held under the district system.

title: Democrats win county offices on the November 2026 ballot (unofficial)
description: Unofficial returns (county document dated 11/3/2026): Democrats won sheriff, prosecutor, commissioner District 1, clerk, auditor, assessor and council Districts A, B, C, E and H. The Board of Commissioners will be 2-1 Democratic and the County Council 7-2 Democratic from January 2027. WVPE describes the commissioner result as the first Democratic board majority since 2012; county results document a Republican majority each year from 2013 (2009-2012 composition not verified).

title: State investigation of Roseland's 2024 finances filed
description: The State Board of Accounts filed special investigation report 19010I on the Town of Roseland for 2024. It charges former Clerk-Treasurer Shane Williams-Inez $22,141.10 (purchases without a documented town purpose plus investigation costs), lists $38,300.70 in questioned costs, and was forwarded to the Indiana Attorney General and the local prosecutor.
